# Data

**All data is synthetic.** Harvest Box is a fictional UK meal-kit subscription company. The warehouse `data/harvest.db` (SQLite, ~19 MB) is generated by `src/harvest/build_db.py` with a fixed seed (17), so every number in this repo is reproducible:

```bash
PYTHONPATH=src python -m harvest.build_db    # ~30 s, writes data/harvest.db
```

`data/*.db` is **git-ignored** (regenerate it with the command above). The analysis outputs in `results/` and the Power BI CSVs in `powerbi/` are committed, so you can read the findings or build the dashboard without running Python.

## Why synthetic
Real subscription data (customers, cancellations, marketing spend, web events) is commercially sensitive and personal, so no realistic open equivalent exists. The generator plants known patterns (cohort decay, better retention for referrals, a winter peak, a checkout A/B effect, Pareto-shaped recipe demand) and **deliberate data-quality problems**, so the SQL can be checked against a known truth. The schema mirrors what you would find in a real meal-kit or subscription-box warehouse; to use real data, load your tables with the same names and columns and every query in `sql/` runs unchanged.

## Schema (star schema)

| Table | Grain | Rows | Columns |
|---|---|---|---|
| `dim_customers` | customer | 12,000 | `customer_id`, `signup_date`, `region` (8 UK regions), `acquisition_channel` (paid_social, search, referral, tv, affiliate_voucher), `plan_id`, `age_band` |
| `dim_plans` | plan | 4 | `plan_id`, `plan_name`, `people`, `recipes_per_box`, `weekly_price_gbp` (£41.99–£79.99) |
| `dim_recipes` | recipe | 60 | `recipe_id`, `recipe_name`, `cuisine` (8), `ingredient_cost_gbp` (per person), `cook_minutes` |
| `fact_orders` | weekly box | 124,437 raw (121,369 after cleaning) | `order_id`, `customer_id`, `delivery_date`, `plan_id`, `status` (delivered / refunded), `revenue_gbp`, `discount_gbp` |
| `fact_order_items` | recipe in a box | 423,648 | `order_id`, `recipe_id` |
| `fact_cancellations` | cancellation | 10,422 | `customer_id`, `cancel_date`, `reason` (6 reasons) |
| `fact_events` | web event | 60,326 (26,000 sessions, 12,318 visitors) | `session_id`, `visitor_id`, `event_time`, `event_name` (landing → menu → plan_select → checkout → purchase), `device`, `ab_variant` |
| `fact_marketing` | channel × month | 150 | `month` (2024-01 to 2026-06), `channel`, `spend_gbp` |

Period: deliveries from 3 January 2024 to 28 June 2026 (30 months). Web events cover the 12-week A/B test from 6 April 2026.

## Planted data-quality problems (found by `sql/01_data_quality_checks.sql`)
- 15 duplicated order rows
- 8 orders with missing revenue
- 5 orders for a customer ID that doesn't exist

`sql/02_clean_orders_view.sql` creates the view `v_orders` (de-duplicated, known customers, revenue present, delivered only), which every later query uses.

## How the data is generated (summary)
- **Sign-ups** grow over time with a January spike; channel mix 35% paid social, 26% search, 15% referral, 15% affiliate vouchers, 9% TV.
- **Orders**: one box per week, with pauses (more in summer, fewer in winter). Weekly churn probability is 5.5% divided by a channel retention multiplier (referral 1.35, affiliate vouchers 0.55) and higher in the first two weeks. First boxes are discounted 25% (50% for voucher customers). 2.5% of boxes are refunded.
- **Recipes** are chosen with Pareto-distributed popularity.
- **Web sessions**: step-to-step conversion depends on device (mobile lowest); variant B multiplies checkout → purchase by 1.12.
- **Marketing spend** = sign-ups × a channel cost per acquisition (referral £15 … TV £70) × random noise of ±15%.

## Power BI export
`python -m harvest.export_powerbi` turns this database into star-schema CSVs in `powerbi/` (fact and dimension tables, a date dimension, consistent integer keys, ISO dates). See [powerbi/README.md](../powerbi/README.md) and [powerbi/data_dictionary.md](../powerbi/data_dictionary.md).

## Personal data
There are no real people in this data. In a real warehouse `dim_customers` and `fact_events` would be personal data under UK GDPR: see the Responsible AI section of the main README.
